content: Those who know do not speak; those who speak do not know. Close your mouth, blunt your sharpness, untie your knots, soften your glare.
author: Lao Tzu
sourceWork: Tao Te Ching (Dao De Jing), Book of the Way
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Loneliness is the painful ache of feeling incomplete, while solitude is the rich discovery of your own inner presence. In a world full of constant stimulation and notifications, being alone with your thoughts can feel intimidating.

Across his life and work, Lao Tzu saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Yet silence is the only space where you can hear what your life is actually trying to say to you. When you make peace with quiet, you stop running to distractions to save you from yourself.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
